files.lesson.md: --- order: 8 unit: lines node: AC9M8A02 n1 title: Lines and regions summary: "y = 2x + 1 is a line; y < 2x + 1 is every point below it. Draw the boundary (dashed if points on it are not included, solid if they are), then test a point to see which side to shade. Vertical lines are x = a; horizontal lines are y = a." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A delivery zone, a speed limit, a budget: often the answer is not one point but a whole region of points that work." connection: load-limit # data/connections/maths.yml app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8176 url: http://127.0.0.1:8176/index.html readySelector: "#legend" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: graph.yml#explain, caption: "$y < 2x + 1$: below the dashed line. $O(0, 0)$ is in it ($0 < 1$); $A(1, 4)$ is not ($4 < 3$ is false)." } explainClip: query: { code: "@graph.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "A line, then a region" say: "An inequality is a region: every point that makes it true." clip: - caption: { text: "The boundary is y = 2x + 1. Dashed: for <, points on it are not included.", say: "The boundary is the line. It is dashed, so the line itself is not included." } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Test O (0, 0): 0 < 2 × 0 + 1 is true, so shade O's side.", say: "Test a point. Zero is less than one: true, so shade that side." } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Test A (1, 4): 4 < 3 is false. A is outside.", say: "Four is not less than three, so A is outside." } - wait: 1400 --- You can graph a line from its rule, such as $y = 2x + 1$. Now: what about $y < 2x + 1$? Every point whose $y$ is less than $2x + 1$ makes it true, and those points fill a whole **region** of the graph. You also meet lines with only one letter: $x = 3$ (vertical) and $y = -2$ (horizontal). ## Predict: in or out? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to whether (1, 4) satisfies y < 2x + 1 shows whether they substitute both coordinates, before the board shows the region." check: type: predict q: "Is the point $(1, 4)$ in the region $y < 2x + 1$?" options: - "No: 4 is not less than 2 × 1 + 1 = 3" - "Yes: 4 is bigger than 1" - "It is on the boundary line" actual: "No. Put x = 1 and y = 4 in: is 4 < 3? No. (1, 4) is above the line, outside the region." ``` Put $x = 1$ and $y = 4$ into $y < 2x + 1$. Is it true? ## Run: into the region ```step stage: run insight: "Dragging P into the shaded region and reading its coordinates shows that every point there makes the inequality true, and the boundary is not included for <." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Drag $P$ into the shaded region $y < 2x + 1$. Check its coordinates in the inequality. Was your prediction right about $(1, 4)$?", when: "y(P) < 2 * x(P) + 1" } ``` Try a point on the dashed line too. Does it make $y < 2x + 1$ true? ## Investigate: boundary, then test ```step stage: investigate insight: "Draw the boundary (dashed for < and >, solid for ≤ and ≥), test a point not on it, and shade the side that makes it true. Ana's mistake draws a strict inequality's boundary solid." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#two", height: 600 } tasks: - check: type: question q: "For $y \\ge x - 2$, is the boundary line solid or dashed?" options: ["Solid: ≥ includes the points on the line", "Dashed: points on the line are not included", "There is no boundary"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "≥ means greater than or equal to, so the line's points count.", "Every region of this kind is bounded by the line y = x − 2."] explain: "≤ and ≥ include the boundary (solid); < and > do not (dashed)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ana" text: "Ana graphs $y > x + 1$. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: boundary-solid explain: "Line 2: > does not include the line itself, so the boundary is dashed. Her test and shading are right." - starter: "graph.yml#two" hint: ["The orange region is x ≥ 3: on or right of x = 3.", "The other is y < 2: below the dashed line y = 2."] check: { type: board, text: "Two regions: $x \\ge 3$ and $y < 2$. Drag $P$ to a point that is in both.", when: "x(P) >= 3 and y(P) < 2", explain: "Any point with x at least 3 and y below 2, such as (4, 0)." } ``` ### Boundary and test Here is how to graph an inequality. ```worked y < 2x + 1 :: The boundary is the line $y = 2x + 1$. \text{dashed} :: $<$ does not include the line's points (for $\le$ or $\ge$, draw it solid). (0, 0):\; 0 < 2 \times 0 + 1 :: Test a point not on the line. $0 < 1$ is true. \text{shade the side with } (0, 0) :: True: shade the test point's side. (False: shade the other side.) x = 3,\; y = -2 :: One letter: $x = 3$ is vertical (every point has $x$ = 3); $y = -2$ is horizontal. ``` Solid or dashed for $y \ge x - 2$? ### Find the mistake Read Ana's working. Which line does not match the sign? ### Two regions at once ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: vertical and horizontal lines, reading an inequality from its region, a point on a solid boundary, a point on a dashed one, then a region with no x in it." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#cross", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "graph.yml#cross" hint: "x = −2 is the vertical line; y = 3 the horizontal one." check: { type: board, text: "Drag $P$ to where $x = -2$ meets $y = 3$.", when: "x(P) = -2 and y(P) = 3", explain: "(−2, 3): on x = −2 (x is −2) and on y = 3 (y is 3)." } - picture: { ref: graph.yml#which-pic, caption: "A shaded region with a solid boundary." } check: type: question q: "Which inequality is shaded?" options: ["$y \\ge -x + 2$", "$y > -x + 2$", "$y \\le -x + 2$", "$y \\ge x + 2$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The boundary is solid, so it is ≥.", "The shading is above the line.", "The line goes down: its gradient is −1."] explain: "The line y = −x + 2 (down 1 for each step right, through (0, 2)), solid, shaded above: y ≥ −x + 2." - starter: "graph.yml#edge" hint: "On the line: y = 4 − x. The boundary is solid, so those points count." check: { type: board, text: "The region is $y \\le -x + 4$. Drag $P$ to a point on its boundary line.", when: "y(P) = 4 - x(P)", explain: "Points on y = −x + 4, such as (1, 3), are in the region: ≤ includes the line." } - check: type: question q: "Is $(2, 5)$ in the region $y > 2x + 1$?" options: ["No: 5 > 5 is false, so it is on the dashed boundary, not in the region", "Yes: 5 is more than 2", "Yes: it is on the line"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Use both coordinates: 2 × 2 + 1 = 5.", "On a dashed line means not included."] explain: "2 × 2 + 1 = 5, and 5 > 5 is false: the point is on the boundary, which > leaves out." - picture: { ref: graph.yml#below-pic, caption: "The region $y < 3$." } check: type: question q: "Edge case: which points are in $y < 3$?" options: ["Every point below the horizontal line y = 3, whatever its x", "Only points with x less than 3", "Only the point (0, 3)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "There is no x in y < 3: only y matters.", "That point is on the boundary, which < leaves out."] explain: "x can be anything; y must be less than 3: the half below the dashed line y = 3." ``` ### Vertical and horizontal Each task changes one thing. ### Read the region ### On a solid boundary ### On a dashed boundary ### No x ## Practise: regions ```step stage: practise insight: "Testing points, choosing boundaries and reading lines, mixed; the solid-dashed slip planted again; the review keeps gradient and intercept fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Which point is in $y \\le 3x - 2$?" options: ["$(2, 1)$", "$(0, 1)$", "$(1, 3)$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "1 ≤ −2 is false.", "3 ≤ 1 is false."] explain: "(2, 1): 1 ≤ 3 × 2 − 2 = 4. True." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Try a different point first: when $x = 4$, what is $3x - 2$?", answer: 10, explain: "3 × 4 − 2 = 10. So at x = 4 the line is at 10, and a point there is in the region if its y is 10 or less." } - check: type: question q: "Which has a dashed boundary?" options: ["$x < -1$", "$x \\le -1$", "$y \\ge 2x$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "≤ includes the line: solid.", "≥ includes the line: solid."] explain: "< and > leave the line out: dashed." - check: type: question q: "Which line is vertical?" options: ["$x = 4$", "$y = 4$", "$y = 4x$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "y = 4 is horizontal: every point has y = 4.", "y = 4x goes through the origin, up 4 for each step right."] explain: "x = 4: every point has x = 4, so the points stack straight up: a vertical line." - check: type: question q: "Review: what are the gradient and y-intercept of $y = 3x - 2$?" options: ["Gradient 3, y-intercept −2", "Gradient −2, y-intercept 3", "Gradient 3, y-intercept 2"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "m is the number in front of x.", "The intercept keeps its sign: −2."] explain: "y = mx + c with m = 3 and c = −2." ``` ### Test a point ### Solid or dashed ### Vertical ### Review: m and c ## Make: fit the region ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing m and c so a region contains some points and not others reverses the lesson: from points to the inequality." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#make", height: 620 } hint: ["(0, 0) in y ≤ mx + c means 0 ≤ c.", "(0, 3) outside means c is less than 3. Then check B (2, 1): 1 ≤ 2m + c."] check: { type: board, text: "Set $m$ and $c$ so the region $y \\le mx + c$ contains $A(0, 0)$ and $B(2, 1)$ but not $C(0, 3)$.", when: "c >= 0 and c < 3 and 2m + c >= 1", explain: "For example m = 1, c = 0: y ≤ x contains (0, 0) and (2, 1), and 3 ≤ 0 is false for C." } ``` Find two different answers. What do they have in common? ## Make: trailer load, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A load limit is a boundary: every load at or under it works. The inequality gives a number of boxes, and the situation, not the calculator, decides how to round it." hint: ["The total is the mower plus 40 for each box, and it may not go over 750.", "n is a whole number of boxes: what happens at 17?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A trailer is rated for 750 kg and already carries a 90 kg mower. Each box of pavers is 40 kg. On paper, write an inequality for n boxes, solve it, and say the most whole boxes that can go on." steps: - ["$90 + 40n \\le 750$", "the total may be 750 kg or less, so the limit itself is allowed"] - ["$40n \\le 660$, so $n \\le 16.5$", "take 90 from both sides, then divide by 40"] - ["Boxes come whole. 17 boxes would be $90 + 680 = 770$ kg, over the limit, so the most is 16", "round down, because rounding up breaks the limit"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Why is the inequality ≤ and not Do the Run board and the Make task yourself first. Students need Lines and their rules (gradient and intercept). The one idea: an inequality is every point that makes it true; the line is its boundary, dashed when the line's points are left out (< and >) and solid when they are in (≤ and ≥). The common mistake is the wrong boundary style; it is planted in Ana's working. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose yes compared 4 with 1, not with 2 × 1 + 1." - "Run: ask students to read out a point in the region and check it aloud." - "Investigate: model the boundary-then-test routine with (0, 0); ask when (0, 0) would be a bad test point (when it is on the line)." - "Modify: before the vertical line task, ask what every point on x = −2 has in common." - "Make: collect students' m and c and test C in each." - "Paper: the trailer task in Make is worked in books; the page marks the number (16) and both reasons. Books out, then check 16 and 17 boxes against 750 kg." stuck: - see: A student draws the boundary solid for < (Ana's mistake). ask: Does a point on the line make y < 2x + 1 true? fix: "No (it makes the two sides equal), so the line is not included: dashed." - see: A student shades the wrong side. ask: Which point did you test? Was the result true or false? fix: "True: shade the test point's side. False: the other side." - see: A student draws x = 3 horizontally. ask: Name three points with x = 3. fix: "(3, 0), (3, 1), (3, −2): they line up vertically." stretch: Shade the region where y ≥ x and y < 4 and x > 0 (a triangle). What are its corners? support: "Use the Run board: drag P and read whether the coordinates make the inequality true." leads: > Next: Solving with graphs, then (in Algebra) Inequalities, which solves one-variable inequalities and checks them graphically. Where it leads: linear programming and simultaneous inequalities (Years 10 and up). exit: q: Graph y ≥ −2x + 3 (describe the boundary and the side). Is (1, 1) in it? a: "Solid line through (0, 3), down 2 for each step right; shade above. (1, 1): 1 ≥ 1, true: on the boundary, so in." explain: > **One-letter lines**: $x = 3$ is vertical (every point has $x = 3$); $y = -2$ is horizontal. An **inequality** such as $y < 2x + 1$ is a **region**: every point that makes it true. To graph it: 1. Draw the boundary line $y = 2x + 1$: **dashed** for $<$ and $>$ (its points are not included), **solid** for $\le$ and $\ge$. 2. Test a point not on the line, often $(0, 0)$: $0 < 1$ is true. 3. Shade the side of the test point if it was true, the other side if it was false. ```
files.graph.yml:
# Graph boards for "Lines and regions". shade: draws a region with its boundary (dashed for < and >, solid for ≤ and ≥).

# region: run
widget: graph
x: -4, 5
y: -5, 8
shade: y < 2x + 1
point P: 1, 4, drag
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: graph
x: -4, 5
y: -5, 8
shade: y < 2x + 1
point O: 0, 0
point A: 1, 4
# endregion

# region: two
widget: graph
x: -2, 7
y: -4, 6
shade: x >= 3
shade: y < 2
point P: 0, 4, drag
# endregion

# region: cross
widget: graph
x: -5, 5
y: -5, 6
plot: x = -2
plot: y = 3
point P: 2, -2, drag
# endregion

# region: which-pic
widget: graph
x: -4, 5
y: -4, 7
shade: y >= -x + 2
# endregion

# region: edge
widget: graph
x: -4, 6
y: -4, 7
shade: y <= -x + 4
point P: 0, -2, drag
# endregion

# region: below-pic
widget: graph
x: -4, 5
y: -4, 6
shade: y < 3
# endregion

# region: make
widget: graph
x: -4, 5
y: -5, 6
slider m: -3, 3, 0
slider c: -5, 5, -2
shade: y <= mx + c
point A: 0, 0
point B: 2, 1
point C: 0, 3
# endregion
